hook.en: Two machines fill 1-litre milk packets. Both average 1 litre, but is one of them more erratic? To compare two variances we take their ratio, and that ratio follows the F distribution, named after R. A. Fisher.
hook.kn: ಎರಡು ಯಂತ್ರಗಳು 1 ಲೀಟರ್ ಹಾಲಿನ ಪೊಟ್ಟಣಗಳನ್ನು ತುಂಬುತ್ತವೆ. ಎರಡರ ಸರಾಸರಿ 1 ಲೀಟರ್, ಆದರೆ ಒಂದು ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಅಸ್ಥಿರವೇ? ಎರಡು ಪ್ರಸರಣಗಳ ಅನುಪಾತ F ವಿತರಣೆ ಹೊಂದುತ್ತದೆ; ಇದು ಆರ್. ಎ. ಫಿಶರ್ ಹೆಸರಿನದು.

objectives.en: State its properties and the reciprocal property

narration.en: Two machines fill 1-litre milk packets. Both average 1 litre, but is one of them more erratic? To compare two variances we take their ratio, and that ratio follows the F distribution, named after R. A. Fisher.
narration.kn: ಎರಡು ಯಂತ್ರಗಳು 1 ಲೀಟರ್ ಹಾಲಿನ ಪೊಟ್ಟಣಗಳನ್ನು ತುಂಬುತ್ತವೆ. ಎರಡರ ಸರಾಸರಿ 1 ಲೀಟರ್, ಆದರೆ ಒಂದು ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಅಸ್ಥಿರವೇ? ಎರಡು ಪ್ರಸರಣಗಳ ಅನುಪಾತ F ವಿತರಣೆ ಹೊಂದುತ್ತದೆ; ಇದು ಆರ್. ಎ. ಫಿಶರ್ ಹೆಸರಿನದು.

body.en: If $\chi^2_1$ and $\chi^2_2$ are independent chi-square variates with $n_1$ and $n_2$ d.f., then $F = \dfrac{\chi^2_1/n_1}{\chi^2_2/n_2}$ follows the F distribution with $(n_1, n_2)$ d.f. For two independent samples from normal populations with equal variances, $F = s_1^2/s_2^2$ with $(n_1 - 1, n_2 - 1)$ d.f.
body.kn: ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ χ²₁ (n₁ d.f.) ಮತ್ತು χ²₂ (n₂ d.f.) ಆದರೆ F = (χ²₁/n₁)/(χ²₂/n₂) ಗೆ (n₁, n₂) ಸ್ವಾತಂತ್ರ್ಯ ಮಟ್ಟಗಳ F ವಿತರಣೆ. ಮಾದರಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ F = s₁²/s₂².

points.en: Ratio of two independent χ²s, each divided by its d.f.

narration.en: If chi-square_1 and chi-square_2 are independent chi-square variates with n_1 and n_2 d.f., then F = dfracchi-square_1/n_1chi-square_2/n_2 follows the F distribution with (n_1, n_2) d.f. For two independent samples from normal populations with equal variances, F = s_1^2/s_2^2 with (n_1 - 1, n_2 - 1) d.f.
narration.kn: ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ χ²₁ (n₁ d.f.) ಮತ್ತು χ²₂ (n₂ d.f.) ಆದರೆ F = (χ²₁/n₁)/(χ²₂/n₂) ಗೆ (n₁, n₂) ಸ್ವಾತಂತ್ರ್ಯ ಮಟ್ಟಗಳ F ವಿತರಣೆ. ಮಾದರಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ F = s₁²/s₂².

narration.en: The teacher writes the definition, draws the F(5, 10) curve and links F with t and chi-square.

say.en: F is a ratio of two independent chi-squares, each divided by its degrees of freedom.
Here is the F curve for 5 and 10 degrees of freedom. It starts at zero, rises and has a long right tail.
Its mean depends only on the denominator d.f.: n2 over n2 minus 2. For F(5, 10) that is 1.25.
Swap the d.f. and take the reciprocal: that gives the lower percentage point.
And t squared is F with 1 and n degrees of freedom.

body.en: F ranges from 0 to $\infty$ and is positively skewed. Mean $= \dfrac{n_2}{n_2 - 2}$ ($n_2 > 2$). Reciprocal property: $F_{1-\alpha}(n_2, n_1) = 1/F_{\alpha}(n_1, n_2)$. Relations: $t_n^2 = F(1, n)$ and, as $n_2 \to \infty$, $n_1 F \to \chi^2_{n_1}$. Application: testing the equality of two population variances (and analysis of variance).
body.kn: F 0 ಯಿಂದ ∞, ಧನಾತ್ಮಕ ವಿಷಮ. ಸರಾಸರಿ n₂/(n₂ − 2). ವ್ಯುತ್ಕ್ರಮ ಗುಣ. t²ₙ = F(1, n). ಎರಡು ಪ್ರಸರಣಗಳ ಸಮಾನತೆಯ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಗೆ ಬಳಕೆ.

narration.en: F ranges from 0 to infty and is positively skewed. Mean = dfracn_2n_2 - 2 (n_2 > 2). Reciprocal property: F_1-alpha(n_2, n_1) = 1/F_alpha(n_1, n_2). Relations: t_n^2 = F(1, n) and, as n_2 to infty, n_1 F to chi-square_n_1. Application: testing the equality of two population variances (and analysis of variance).

caption.en: F density with (n₁, n₂) d.f. Slide both degrees of freedom.

narration.en: Change the numerator and denominator degrees of freedom. With more degrees of freedom the F curve gathers more tightly around 1.

tryThis.en: Increase n₂. Does the mean approach 1?
Set n₁ = 1 or 2: where is the peak?
Make both d.f. large. What happens to the spread?

problem.en: The upper 5% point of F(5, 10) is 3.33. Find the lower 5% point of F(10, 5), and the mean of F(5, 10).

narration.en: Let us work this out together. The upper 5% point of F(5, 10) is 3.33. Find the lower 5% point of F(10, 5), and the mean of F(5, 10).

body.en: F(n₁, n₂): numerator first, denominator second. The mean depends only on the denominator d.f. (the "bottom" one): n₂/(n₂ − 2).

narration.en: Which d.f. comes first?. F(n₁, n₂): numerator first, denominator second. The mean depends only on the denominator d.f. (the "bottom" one): n₂/(n₂ − 2).

mnemonic.en: Top first, bottom decides the mean
